findings.title: Canonical event serialization is ambiguous for delimiter-bearing fields
findings.evidence: serialize_canonical concatenates event_id, comma-joined parents, tick, payload and signature using unescaped delimiters.
findings.trigger: Two otherwise identical events with payload/signature pairs (a|b,c) and (a,b|c).
findings.impact: Both serialize to the same canonical bytes and graph digest despite different event content; the reference cannot serve as an integrity oracle.

findings.title: Exported global hash does not bind artifact state
findings.evidence: global_hash is SHA256 of the constant bytes artifact_state_v3; program and canonical_graph are not included.
findings.trigger: Export different programs or ledger states through B60MinimalVM.export_artifact.
findings.impact: Every manifest has the same global_hash, preventing consumers of this example field from detecting artifact substitution.

findings.title: Reference CLI announces proof dispatch that never occurs
findings.evidence: static_proof at lines 114-116 is pass; export_artifact returns only in-memory values, while CLI prints Proof IR extracted. Dispatched to Lean/Coq Backends.
findings.impact: Example output misrepresents absent formal verification as completed proof generation and dispatch. No production proof bypass is alleged.

findings.title: FD exhaustion test also passes when target operation succeeds
findings.evidence: Descriptor duplication stops after 5001 even if exhaustion was not reached; the only result assertion is inside if let Err(e) = res.
findings.trigger: Run with a soft descriptor limit above the fixed duplication cap.
findings.impact: Test can report success without entering EMFILE or validating failure under actual exhaustion, leaving the named failure path untested.

findings.title: BLE discovery filters on characteristic UUID instead of advertised service
findings.evidence: Architecture line 29 identifies service 0000180d... and characteristic 00002a37...; scanner instead searches service_uuids for HR_MEASUREMENT_UUID (00002a37...).
findings.trigger: A standard heart-rate device advertises the 0x180d service described by this same document.
findings.impact: The supplied daemon example does not discover the intended device and returns Emisor no encontrado.

findings.title: Cross-device rejection test compares a device ID with itself
findings.evidence: test_nemesis_v12_mount_boundary_exdev_fail_closed asserts q.dev == q.dev and checks only the display string of a constructed CrossDeviceUnsupported error. It never supplies a different mount or invokes an operation expected to return EXDEV.
findings.trigger: A regression removes cross-device rejection from the backend.
findings.impact: This named security regression test still passes because none of its assertions exercise the rejection behavior.

findings.title: Concurrent revocation test asserts a locally manufactured abort
findings.evidence: The revocation thread stores true and is joined before the branch; the true branch constructs EffectTxState::Aborted and asserts it equals itself. It neither revokes an orchestrator authority nor dispatches a guarded operation.
findings.trigger: A regression disables actual revocation enforcement.
findings.impact: test_nemesis_v09_concurrent_capability_revocation remains green without testing revocation or any concurrent operation against the orchestrator. The simulation is labelled in a comment but cannot support the suite security-coverage claim.

hypotheses.description: Digest validation accepts any nonempty 64-character value other than the empty SHA256, including nonhex strings. This weakens the proposed model schema; no effect consumer was found in the targeted verification package search, so no execution or authorization bypass is asserted.

coverage.notes: Entire file statically reviewed in chunks of at most 200 lines; no execution.

tool_limitations: Native codebase graph tools were not exposed; discovery used bounded text reads and targeted rg.
Initial combined read output was truncated; affected small files were subsequently reread in bounded groups.
No repository code, tests, build, runtime, external API verification, commits or push were executed.
Frozen shard SHA256 values matched all 25 assigned paths; no symlinks among assigned paths.
